system.concept: Tremere High Regent of the Annex at the Kenilworth
system.title: High Regent, Kenilworth Chantry
system.biography:
Background

Born a dwarf in nineteenth-century England, Ephraim Wainwright was ghouled and then Embraced by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Aidan Lyle after proving his mastery of Thaumaturgical theory. A scholar's scholar with a reputation for apocalyptic writing (his Songs of the Eve of Gehenna scandalized both @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} elders alike), Wainwright now presides over the Annex at the Kenilworth, the largest of New York's satellite chantries, where his Kenilworth thaumaturges have lately turned their study toward rituals — including Blood Into Water, Luminous Vitae, and Obscure the Malice — that shore up the Masquerade in the war's aftermath. Secretly tasked by Vienna to engineer High Regent Aisling Sturbridge's downfall, Wainwright resents answering to both Sturbridge and the upstart Eugenio Estevez.

Roleplaying Hints

You tolerate no dissent from those beneath you and consider undermining Sturbridge a matter of clan discipline, not treachery. Younger Tremere's fondness for “technomancies” and other bastard sorceries offends you personally.
system.notes: Sire: Aidan Lyle. Thaumaturgical Paths (Storyteller discretion): Path of Blood 5, Alchemy 5, Lure of Flames 5, Movement of the Mind 5, Path of Conjuring 5, Countermagic 4, The Hearth Path 4, Elemental Mastery 3, Spirit Manipulation 3, Focused Mind 2. Secretly tasked by Vienna to unseat Aisling Sturbridge. Ratings above 5 from the original stat block have been capped to fit this system's 1-5 scale.

items.name: Thaumaturgy (Path of Blood) — 3 Advanced — Cauldron of Blood

system.description: By winning a Physical Challenge to grasp your target, you spend up to three Mental Traits to boil that many of the victim's Blood Traits, each inflicting one level of aggravated damage.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

items.name: Thaumaturgy (Path of Blood) — 2 Intermediate — Blood of Potency

system.description: By concentrating your vitae for the scene or an hour, you spend two Mental Traits per generation (up to three generations) to gain a temporary, more potent virtual generation, raising your Blood Trait maximum and Dominate's reach.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: You draw on the strength of the earth or nearby objects to enhance your body, immediately gaining three strength-related Physical Traits of your choice without needing to spend blood. You may activate this power and attack in the same turn. The Traits last for a number of turns equal to your rating in Elemental Mastery, and you may spend a Willpower Trait for one additional turn. This power cannot be stacked; the first application must expire before it can be used again.
system.duration: Turns equal to Elemental Mastery rating

system.description: Maintain physical contact with an object or location and concentrate for a turn, expending a Mental Trait, then ask the Narrator one question about who last touched it, whether it was involved in stressful situations, or what strong emotions drove its user. May be used repeatedly for greater insight; objects of powerful emotional resonance may force a derangement upon the user for the scene.

By this gift, a Toreador may penetrate the "soul" of an inanimate artwork she examines, interpreting the piece, gleaning the artist's state of mind, the relationship between artist and work, and the stages of the creative process, revealed as a series of progressively paler images looking back into the work's history. Some Toreador use this to critique or authenticate a piece; others monitor their proteges' work for unspoken rebellion or sadness, or seek the "real" story behind a letter proposing an alliance. The power does not function on "living" art still in the act of performance — a play, a song, or a story being told — since such work depends on the performer's ongoing intent rather than a fixed, finished creation.

System: The character examines the work and the number of successes determines how much she perceives: a single success yields only general feelings with no historical context; two successes offer a vague sense of the work's history; three successes reveal specific details and a fuzzy timeline; four successes grant a definite sense of the artist's emotional state and a reasonable timeline; five successes let the Toreador see the work in stages, feeling what the artist felt at every step of its creation. The difficulty rises for pieces with multiple artists or a long creation span; examining something as vast as a cathedral or castle risks leaving the Toreador a gibbering wreck from informational overload.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book One: Artisans (Toreador)

system.description: By meeting your subject's gaze and winning a Mental Challenge, you implant a more complex command, optionally tied to a specific trigger event, to be carried out immediately or later.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

system.description: By meeting your subject's gaze and speaking a single emphasized word of command, you win a Mental Challenge to force immediate, unquestioning obedience to a simple order lasting no more than ten minutes.
system.source: Laws of the Night Revised, Disciplines

vtmlarp.source: New York by Night, 2nd Edition, Chapter Three: All the Beautiful Monsters
